text: Problem set 6 Problem 1. (i) Let T : V → W be invertible. Show that T t is invertible and (T t)−1 = (T −1)t. (ii) Let A ∈ Mn×n(F ) be an invertible matrix. Show that if A is symmetric then A−1 is also symmetric and if A is anti-symmetric, then A−1 is also anti-symmetric. Problem 2. Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field F and W ⊂ V be a subspace . (i) Let φ ∈ W ∗ and (w1, . . . , wm) be a basis for W . We extend (w1, . . . , wm) to a basis (w1, . . . , wm, vm+1, . . . , vn) of V . We define ˜φ : V → F by specifying its values on the basis: ˜φ(wi) = φ(wi) for i = 1, . . . , m and ˜φ(vj) = 0 for j = m + 1, . . . , n. Show that ˜φ(w) = φ(w) for any w ∈ W . (ii) Let i : W ∗ → V ∗ be the map defined by i(φ) = ˜φ. Show that i is an injective linear map. (iii) Let φ1, . . . , φn be the dual basis of w1, . . . , wm, vm+1, . . . , vn. Show that i(W ∗) = span(φ1, . . . , φm) and W ⊥ = span(φm+1, . . . , φn). (iv) Show that V ∗ = i(W ∗) ⊕ W ⊥. Remark 1. i(W ∗) is like the mirror of W in V ∗ and W ⊥ is the complement of i(W ∗) in V ∗. Problem 3. Let A =  1 1 0 0 1 1 1 2 1   , B = A t =   1 0 1 1 1 2 0 1 1   . Find the RREF of A and B. Problem 4. Let T : V → W be a linear transformation and X ⊂ W be a subspace. (i) Show that T −1(X) = {v ∈ V : T (v) ∈ X} is a subspace of V . (ii) Let w1, . . . , wk ∈ X be a basis of X ∩ im(T ) and v1, . . . , vk ∈ V be such that T (vi) = wi for all i = 1, . . . , k. Show that T −1(X) = span(v1, . . . , vk) ⊕ ker(T ). (iii) Show that dim T −1(X) = dim V + dim X − dim(X + im(T )). Hint: You need to show that v1, . . . , vk in (ii) are linearly independent. (iv) The codimension of a subspace X ⊂ W is defined to be dim W − dim X. A linear transformation T is transversal to X if X + im(T ) = W . Show that (iii) implies that if if T is transversal to X, then the codimension of X is equal to the codimension of T −1(X). 1
